UX-A11Y-003.how: Both halves. (a) Each shelf entry is now `<button type="button" class="pick" data-shelf=N>` instead of `<label data-shelf=N>`, and the handler loop selects `#shelf button[data-shelf]`; a new `ul.todo button.pick` rule plus a `:focus-visible` outline keeps it looking like the list item it replaced. (b) The page image carries `role="button" tabindex="0"` and a `keydown` handler. The click handler was refactored into a shared `readerPress(fx, fy)` taking fractional coordinates, so mouse and keyboard provably enter the same code path; Enter and Space press the middle of the page, which is what a Kindle centre tap does. The handler calls stopPropagation so it does not double up with the signed-out typing route, and arrows are deliberately left to bubble so goal-loop item 2C.3 (arrow keys turn pages) still holds.

The `<label data-shelf>` half of this finding is the same change recorded under UX-A11Y-003.

UX-A11Y-007.how: `role="status" aria-live="polite"` added to `#status` (the footer line say() rewrites after every fetch) and to `#reader-status` (the loading overlay line readerSay() rewrites), and to the `.signin-status` div that renderSignIn() builds, matching the live-region pattern the companions banner and the latency chip already used.

UX-ANIM-001.how: The `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block gained `.bar > i { transition: none; }` next to the existing `.shimmer, .spinner` rule, with a comment saying that any future transition over about 200ms belongs in the same list. The progress bar was the only transition in the file long enough to matter.

UX-CONT-003.how:
loadQueued() now branches on `queued.length`: with items it renders the same list it always did, and with none it renders `
  • Nothing queued yet. What you write above waits here until you want it.
    • `, using the `.empty` class the other four empty states already use.

UX-FORM-008.how: An inline `<div class="err" id="box-err" role="alert" hidden>` sits directly after `#box`, and the textarea points at it through `aria-describedby="box-why box-err"`. A new `boxError(text)` helper fills it, toggles `aria-invalid`, and calls `$('box').focus()`. `savePrompt()`'s silent `if (!text) return;` now says "Write something first. An empty note has nothing to hand off." and puts the cursor back in the box. The save fetch also gained a try/catch (it previously had none, so a daemon refusal threw unhandled) which reports the failure in the same inline place and keeps the typed words. An `input` listener clears the error as soon as the person types, so the complaint does not outlive its cause.
